experiments.name: h1_selection
experiments.question: Does the momentum lookback or the selection cutoff matter, holding exits fixed?

verdict.detail: 3 of 8 qualifying cells sit inside a qualifying neighbourhood (positive and beat random on the same days). Selected the plateau centre (rs_lookback=252, top_pct=0.1, +0.146R) rather than the peak (rs_lookback=21, top_pct=0.1, +0.179R) -- the peak's margin over its neighbours is the part least likely to survive.

experiments.name: h1_entry_delay
experiments.question: Does waiting after the ranking help? Momentum's return is reported absent in the weeks after ranking (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993). Delayed names are re-checked at the last close before the buy and dropped if they no longer rank or trend, so this measures waiting AND re-selection together.

verdict.detail: no configuration of 3 was positive and beat random on the same days. Per docs/03 0.7 rule 4 this is evidence against the hypothesis, not an invitation to widen the search.

experiments.name: h1_trend_filter

verdict.detail: neither arm produced positive expectancy -- trend_filter=True at -0.135R versus trend_filter=False at -0.206R, a gap of +0.071R. The comparison still says which is less bad, but nothing here is selectable.

experiments.name: h1_exit_isolated
experiments.question: With portfolio competition removed so both arms take the same signals, does the stop help or cost?

verdict.detail: use_stop=False at +0.065R versus use_stop=True at -0.033R, a gap of +0.098R, but that gap is 1.5 standard errors on mean per-trade return (paired over 2,259 shared signals, month-clustered) -- under the 2 required.

experiments.name: h2_exit_isolated
experiments.question: With portfolio competition removed so both arms take the same signals, does the stop help or cost?

verdict.detail: use_stop=False at +0.371R versus use_stop=True at -0.045R, a gap of +0.415R, but the arms differ by 29.0% in trade count (19,269 vs 27,146). They did not take the same signals, so this measures exit design and selection together and the gap is not attributable to the exit rule.

experiments.name: h4_exit_isolated
experiments.question: With portfolio competition removed so both arms take the same signals, does the stop help or cost?

verdict.detail: use_stop=False at +0.477R versus use_stop=True at +0.005R, a gap of +0.472R. But the winning arm sits at the 29th percentile against random selection on its own entry dates, so beating the other arm is not evidence of an edge -- both are losing to a coin toss and one loses by less.

experiments.name: h5_exit_isolated
experiments.question: H5 shows +0.055R yet ranks below random selection. With portfolio competition removed so both arms take the same signals, is that the entries or the exit?

verdict.detail: use_stop=False at +0.255R versus use_stop=True at +0.100R, a gap of +0.155R at 2.7 standard errors (paired over 1,918 shared signals, month-clustered), and the winning arm beats random selection on its own entry dates at the 97th percentile. Development split: a question worth pre-registering, not a settled result.
